items.note: Done — there's a search box above the job costing table now. Type any part of a job name and it filters instantly, no page reload. The totals at the bottom update to match what's showing, and it tells you when it's showing a subset rather than the whole company.

Payroll tax is part of it, but not most of it.

Comparing the two: QBO shows $242,406 in direct labor + payroll tax combined; BBM shows $220,525 in Labor. If you add the $27,335 payroll tax onto BBM's number you actually overshoot QBO's combined figure by about $5,455 — so payroll tax alone doesn't cleanly bridge the gap, there's also a real difference in how each side prices labor (hours × rate in BBM vs. what actually posted in QuickBooks).

The bigger piece is materials, not labor: QBO shows $198,053 in Materials, BBM shows $173,719 in Purchase Orders — a $24,333 gap, which is larger than the whole labor difference. That's usually either a material cost posted straight into QuickBooks that was never entered as a PO in BBM, or a PO in BBM that hasn't been billed into QBO yet. Worth checking both directions for Lake Burgen.

There's also $117 in Vehicle expenses + Team meals sitting in QBO that BBM's Expenses line shows as $0 — those are QuickBooks-only entries BBM doesn't pick up at all.

So: check for unposted material bills/POs first — that's the largest single piece — then the labor rate difference. Happy to dig into the specific transactions if you want to pull the detail report.
